summary: A 1934 six-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab on a Skamania County ridge; abandoned in 1952 or later, now gone, with scattered remains and a Forest Service trail past the site.

facts.design: 6-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Gone. The register gives 1952 for abandonment; Willhite says the date is unclear and cites a 1964 image.

access.note: Forest Service trail 140 passes the site. When the Forest Service page was read, the trail was listed as temporarily closed because of the High Lava Fire.

visit.trail_note: Trail 140 is 6.9 miles and runs along the ridge past the site. Nothing stands at the site to climb. The trailhead on Willhite's map is unsigned.

corrections.why: Both detail pages describe a six-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, while the FFLOS index lists the site as ground. A human should decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says abandoned in 1952. Willhite says the date is unclear and cites a 1964 Forest Service image showing the lookout in good condition. The register also captions a 1964 photo. The story gives both.
The register gives 3,465 ft (1,056 m) for the site. FireLookout.com gives 3,495 ft, and the Forest Service uses 3,495 ft for the summit. The record keeps the register's figure.

notes_for_editor: The fate is disputed: the register says 1952, Willhite cites a 1964 image. No staffing or fire history appears in any source read, so none is in the story. The remains come from Willhite's photo captions, not from a visit by us. The Forest Service closure notice is undated in the cache; check it before publishing the access line. The kind correction is low confidence. A WebSearch returned the Forest Service trail page, which was then fetched and quoted directly.
